text:
maria: seeing a spike in tail latency for inference on eu-central-gpu-pool, started ~08:12 UTC. p95 from 80ms -> 320ms.
cluster-bot: [ALERT] gpu_temp_threshold_exceeded on host gnode-17 (gpu0). Temp=98C, throttling=true, XID=13 seen.
jon: which host exactly? can we isolate?
maria: gnode-17 (ip 10.8.17.3), affected gpus 0 and 1. dmesg shows repeated Xid 13 and 'GPU has fallen off the bus' messages. small log snippet:```Apr 28 08:11:42 gnode-17 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00.0): 13, PID=2841     Apr 28 08:11:43 gnode-17 kernel: GPU0: GPU has fallen off the bus.```
sam: I SSH'd in, fan rpm for gpu0 reported 0rpm intermittently, but tool shows fan ok most times. power limit readout was stuck at 150W (should be 300W) until I toggled persistence mode. suspect a firmware/riser power issue.
rachel: are these serving instances on Dedicated or Private? we need to evict only non-pooled critical traffic.
maria: this is Dedicated (rw-dedicated-eu). Rolling fallback to a-quant variant happened automatically, but latency still high for some requests.
jon: immediate plan: 1) cordon gnode-17 from k8s scheduling, 2) drain running pods off GPU devices (grace 60s for critical), 3) offload traffic to warm standby pool. can someone run the drain?
sam: running:```kubectl cordon gnode-17 && kubectl drain gnode-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60```
cluster-bot: [INFO] node gnode-17 cordoned by sam at 08:18 UTC. Pod eviction started.
maria: in parallel I'll try to reset drivers and set power cap back:```ssh root@gnode-17 'nvidia-smi -pm 1; nvidia-smi -pl 300; nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0'``` note: gpu-reset sometimes not supported on Ampere in prod.
sam: tried persistence + pl change, it briefly returned to 300W then dropped back after a few minutes. fan still flapping. suspect hardware (fan header/riser).
jon: ok stop driver resets. don't keep repowering - could destabilize other devices. ops-runbook — post recommended hardware triage steps?
ops-runbook: triage checklist: 1) cordon+drain node (done) 2) confirm RMA tag and schedule physical swap 3) check PSU rail/power telemetry 4) move critical pods to standby, 5) snapshot GPU metrics (temp, fan, power, ECC errs) 6) if Xid>10 persist, mark GPU as flaky and disable in scheduler 7) create support ticket with vendor including dmesg + nvidia-smi logs.
rachel: vendor SLA notes: for Dedicated we have Next Business Day RMA unless safety-critical — ask hw team if this is causing data corruption (ECC errors) to escalate.
maria: grabbed metrics (link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abcd123/gpu-node?from=now-1h). p99 shows latency blip correlating with temp spikes and a handful of ECC corrected errors. snippet from nvidia-smi -q:```Fan Speed                       : 0 %    Performance State           : P2    GPU Current Temp             : 98 C    GPU Current Temp. Max         : 98 C```
sam: I opened a maintenance ticket to replace the card + check riser on gnode-17. Also flagged adjacent gnode-18 since it had intermittent similar warnings last week.
jon: schedule: take node offline for hardware swap now, reroute traffic. If we lose multiple nodes, trigger spillover to eu-west pool. Sam, can you escalate to hw ops to get a replacement slot today?
sam: escalated to hw-ops, they booked a swap window 12:00 UTC but can do emergency at ~09:30 if we sign off.
maria: performance note: observed request-level latency correlates with 'thermal_throttle' metric from runtime. When throttle true, token latency increases ~4x. Need a guard in runtime to prefer cache hits / smaller batch sizes for nodes flagged as throttling. filing follow-up issue.
jon: good. sam — after swap, run burn-in (stress-ng + sample inference) for 30m and watch Xid/ECC. If clear, return to pool with 'node-label gpu-replaced=true' then gradually uncordon.
sam: will do. quick commands I'll run post-swap:```nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/gpu-gnode-17-pre-check.txt stress-ng --gpu 0 --timeout 30m # run sample load python -m inference_benchmark --model redwood-7b --iters 100```
cluster-bot: [INFO] capacity pool eu-central GPUs decreased by 1 due to node drain at 08:20 UTC.
rachel: cost/ops note: repeated fan failures on same rack -> we should consider RMA for whole rack or check PSU distribution before RMA per card.
jon: agree. also add temporary scheduler circuit-breaker: if node reports temp>95C and power cap < 180W, mark as 'hot' and avoid scheduling. Maria open a PR?
maria: opened PR #2743 to add 'hot' avoidance rule and short-circuit large batches on flagged nodes.
sam: swap completed 09:45 UTC. replaced GPU, reseated riser, verified PSU rail voltages. running burn-in now.
cluster-bot: [INFO] node gnode-17 reimaged and under burn-in at 09:51 UTC.
maria: metrics look good so far. no Xid after reseat. fan RPM steady ~2200. p95 back to ~85ms.
jon: thanks team. next steps: 1) confirm RMA for original card, 2) monitor fleet for similar signatures (fan 0rpm + power cap mismatch), 3) add automated detection alert for power-cap vs expected-profile.
ops-runbook: created ticket INFRA-1187 with triage notes + vendor contact.
maria: marking thread resolved after 10:00 UTC if no regressions. :thumbsup:
jon: :thumbsup:
